source.title: Probability Distribution Learning and Its Application in Deep Learning
source.authors: Binchuan Qi; Wei Gong; Li Li

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no truncation or garbling that prevents review.
record.tranche_reason: The paper presents theory and experiments on gradient energy, structure-matrix eigenvalues, and surrogate risk. It does not report training classification error or test any listed version’s named conditions.
record.gate_note: The experiments report surrogate risk and gradient-energy trends, not classification error. The paper mentions random initialization as context but does not compare initialization choices; it also does not test corrupted labels, depth failures, learning-rate stability, or batch normalization. Cited findings from other studies are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes surrogate distribution-fitting risk, gradient energy and structure-matrix eigenvalues. It reports neither training classification error nor comparisons testing the width, depth, initialization, learning-rate stability or normalization effects specified in V1–V6. Its conditional optimization bounds do not establish those effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the optimization conclusion: the authors argue that their PD framework explains SGD optimization through gradient energy and structure-matrix eigenvalues, with experimental support. Their broader conclusion also includes Fenchel–Young loss representation and risk/generalization bounds. They do not report a conclusion that training classification error reaches zero.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes Fenchel-Young-loss training and surrogate-risk dynamics; it does not reproduce the training-error experiments described in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports results across datasets and model architectures, but does not compare the initialization, width, learning-rate, normalization, or shortcut conditions named in the versions.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report decreasing gradient energy and increasing structure-matrix extreme eigenvalues relative to initialization; after those eigenvalues stabilize, surrogate risk decreases monotonically with gradient energy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Across the examined training runs, gradient energy and structure-matrix eigenvalues jointly track surrogate distribution-fitting risk.

record.problems: The CIFAR training-risk results are presented in figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The paper reports surrogate risk, not classification error, and does not report comparisons testing the versions’ key conditions.
record.rows_left_out: Other classical architectures appear in Fig. 5, which reports local Pearson correlations rather than training classification error; the text says correlations converge to 1 across models and datasets but does not supply model-specific numeric results. Related MNIST and Fashion-MNIST plots are outside the named benchmark settings and do not report classification error.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels, and its dependence on capacity, stopping and regularization.
Spurious-minimum frequencies in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction with extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Effects of initialization choices on learning speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.
Recovery or divergence relative to initial stability thresholds, curvature reduction and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch normalization's effects on accuracy gain, training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The custom plain and skip-connected models are evaluated at fixed k=1 in the reported optimization experiments, so they do not test depth degradation. Initialization and shortcut mechanisms are attributed to prior work [11]. Structure-matrix eigenvalues are not loss-Hessian sharpness measurements and do not test V5.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size effects, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual networks’ training error as depth changes; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Initialization comparisons, training speed, trainable depth, and 10,000-layer convolutional training.
Learning rates above or below stability limits, loss rises or divergence, and sharpness behavior.
Batch-normalized versus unnormalized training speed, accuracy, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.
